definition: Defining and managing infrastructure through code that can be stored in version control.
A reusable code component that describes one or more CloudFormation resources and their configuration.
A group of resource definitions that CDK maps to a CloudFormation stack.
Running a CDK app to produce CloudFormation templates and deployment artifacts.
The set of templates and other artifacts produced by CDK synthesis for deployment.
A local file or container image packaged and published for use by deployed infrastructure.
Provisioning storage and roles needed for CDK deployment in an AWS account and Region.
The AWS account and Region where CDK resources are deployed.
An IAM role that an AWS service assumes to perform actions on your behalf.
Key-value settings and cached environment information associated with a CDK construct.
An operation CDK applies to constructs in a scope during synthesis.
A construct and its children to which an operation such as an Aspect applies.
A group of related stacks deployed together in a CDK application.
A group of CDK pipeline stages that can deploy in parallel.
A test that compares a synthesized template with a previously stored baseline.
A test of a specific property or requirement in a generated CloudFormation template.
A difference between deployed resource configuration and its CloudFormation template.
A resource setting that determines what happens to it when its stack is destroyed.
An image used to launch EC2 instances that CDK can look up and cache during synthesis.
A proposed CloudFormation update that can be prepared for review before execution.
A resource definition that lets CloudFormation run custom logic during deployment.
A pipeline that reconfigures itself when its CDK application adds stages or stacks.
An identity that a user, application or service assumes to obtain a set of permissions.
A string that uniquely identifies an AWS resource.
